segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Welcome to Imagination Nights. [pause 3]

Lie down in a way that feels easy. Let the bed take all of your weight. [pause 8]

Breathe in slowly through your nose. And let it out through your mouth, a little longer than it went in. [pause 8]

Again. In. And a long, slow breath out. [pause 10]

Let your forehead go soft. Your jaw. Your shoulders. Your hands. [pause 10]

Now we will relax the body, one part at a time. You do not have to do anything. Just notice each part as I name it, and let it get heavy. [pause 8]

Your feet. Let them be warm and heavy. [pause 15]

Your calves and your knees. Heavy. [pause 15]

Your hips and your lower back. Let them sink. [pause 15]

Your belly. Let it rise and fall on its own. [pause 15]

Your chest. Your shoulders. Your arms, all the way down to your fingertips. [pause 15]

Your neck. Your face. The little muscles around your eyes. [pause 15]

Your whole body, heavy and warm, held by the bed. [pause 15]

There is nothing to do tonight but imagine. And imagining is something you already know how to do. [pause 8]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Tonight's wish is for anyone who dreams of running something of their own. A shop. A salon. A food truck. A small online business. A practice. [pause 11]

When you start something, most of the picture is worry. Money, customers, rules, time. Tonight we step past all that, to a normal working day when the thing is up and running and people are coming. [pause 13]

We are not picturing fame or riches. We are picturing ordinary success. A steady line of people. A regular who knows your name. Enough. [pause 13]

This is a practice of imagination and feeling, not a promise of any result. Keep doing the real work in the daytime, and get good advice when you need it. Tonight is for the feeling of having built something. [pause 13]

If you already run something and it is struggling, you can use this scene too. Picture a good, ordinary day a few months from now, when things have steadied. Picture the bills paid and the regulars coming back. Let your body remember that a business can feel calm. [pause 5]

Picture your business now, however it looks to you. [pause 18]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
It is early morning. You are unlocking the door of your place, or opening your laptop to your shop. [pause 26]

Turn on the lights. Notice the first thing you see. Your name. Your colors. Your things in their places. [pause 29]

Flip the sign to open, or press the button that says live. [pause 29]

The first person of the day arrives. They smile. They have been here before. [pause 29]

Hear them say, I told my sister about you. She is coming next week. [pause 29]

Feel yourself doing the work you are good at. Your hands know what to do. [pause 32]

Midday, there is a little rush. It is busy in the good way. [pause 32]

At closing, you count up the day. It was a good day. Not wild. Just good. Enough to feel steady. [pause 32]

Flip the sign back to closed. Stand for a moment in the quiet room you built. [pause 34]

Say in your mind, this is mine. I made this. [pause 34]

Let the quiet of that room become the quiet of this one. [pause 36]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Now let the scene stay with you as you drift. [pause 10]

You do not have to hold it tightly. Just let it be there, warm and quiet, like a lamp left on in another room. [pause 15]

If your mind wanders, come back to one small detail. A sound. A word. A feeling in your hands. [pause 20]

This is only imagination, and imagination is allowed to be kind. [pause 20]

You might notice that your breathing is slower now than when we began. Let it stay slow. [pause 25]

Let your body grow heavier still. There is nowhere to go. [pause 25]

If you are still awake, that is fine. Lie quietly with the scene, and let the quiet do its work. [pause 30]

Rest now. [pause 60]
